newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-MONACO SIGN CROATIAN STRIKER SPEHAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO SIGN CROATIAN STRIKER SPEHAR.

text.p: French champions Monaco on Thursday signed Croat Robert Spehar from Club Bruges in a reported 200 million Belgian francs ($5.26 million) deal, Bruges said.
"He's been sold," Club Bruges secretary general Jacques De Nolf told Reuters.
"The financial details have been finalised he has been transferred definitively," he said. He declined to reveal the transfer fee.
The French champions wanted Spehar, last year's top scorer in the Belgian first division, to replace Brazil's Sonny Anderson who has gone to Barcelona.
"When I was little I dreamed about playing for a big club like Monaco, also it was my dream to play in the Champions' League," Spehar told Belgian television.
Spehar, who has scored 41 goals in 50 matches since joining before the 1995-1996 season, and Bruges announced last week that the Croat had extended his contract until 2000 on greatly improved terms.
But then Spehar said on Wednesday he had not signed anything. "I didn't sign my contract (with Bruges) and I will not sign the contract," he said.
New Bruges coach Eric Gerets slammed Spehar, the crowd favourite at Bruges, and said he felt used and abused.
"He had given me his word...I've never been so disappointed in anyone, ever," Gerets said.
Bruges director Antoine Van Hove told Belgian newspapers he was considering quitting because of Spehar action.
Spehar hit a hat-trick in Bruges' first match of the new league championship on Saturday.
Spehar did not play for Bruges in their UEFA Cup second preliminary round match against Slovenians HIT Gorica on Tuesday, claiming he had a slight thigh injury.
But Belgian media suggested Spehar's injury had been diplomatic and linked to his expected transfer to Monaco.
Spehar's transfer is the second signing in two days by Monaco. They signed Bosnian defender Muhamed Konjic from Swiss club FC Zurich on Wednesday.
The Bosnian international, voted best defender in Switzerland last season, signed a four-year contract.
